**Claim:** $\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\bigr)=1$.

**Proof.**

The abelian group $\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ carries a natural $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space structure, with scalar multiplication defined on pure tensors by $c\cdot(a\otimes b):=(ca)\otimes b$ (equally well $a\otimes(cb)$; these agree by $\mathbb{Z}$-bilinearity and the divisibility argument below).

Define a map
$$\varphi:\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q},\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto ab,$$
induced from the $\mathbb{Z}$-bilinear map $\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{Q}$, $(a,b)\mapsto ab$. The map $\varphi$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-linear, since $\varphi(c\cdot(a\otimes b))=\varphi(ca\otimes b)=(ca)b=c(ab)=c\,\varphi(a\otimes b)$.

**Surjectivity.** For any $q\in\mathbb{Q}$, the pure tensor $q\otimes 1$ satisfies $\varphi(q\otimes 1)=q\cdot 1=q$.

**Key identity: $a\otimes b=ab\otimes 1$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb{Q}$.** Write $b=m/n$ with $m\in\mathbb{Z}$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Using $\mathbb{Z}$-bilinearity of the tensor product,
$$n\cdot(a\otimes b)=a\otimes(nb)=a\otimes m=m\,(a\otimes 1)=(ma)\otimes 1.$$
On the other hand,
$$n\cdot(ab\otimes 1)=(nab)\otimes 1=(ma)\otimes 1.$$
Hence $n\cdot(a\otimes b)=n\cdot(ab\otimes 1)$. Since $\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space, multiplication by the nonzero integer $n$ is an isomorphism (it is invertible, with inverse given by multiplication by $1/n$). Therefore $a\otimes b=ab\otimes 1$.

**Injectivity.** Any element of $\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ is a finite sum $\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i$. By the identity above,
$$\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i=\sum_i(a_i b_i\otimes 1)=\Bigl(\sum_i a_i b_i\Bigr)\otimes 1.$$
If $\varphi\bigl(\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i\bigr)=\sum_i a_i b_i=0$, then the element equals $0\otimes 1=0$. Thus $\ker\varphi=\{0\}$.

We have shown $\varphi$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear isomorphism $\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\mathbb{Q}$. Hence $\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ is a one-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space (spanned by $1\otimes 1$).

$$\boxed{\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\bigr)=1.}$$
